translation_notes: REVISION of the draft: the draft added "@prefix rdf:"/"@prefix dcterms:" for RDF/DCTERMS, but neither is ever used as a TERM in the extracted lines (no RDF.x, no DCTERMS.x, no MD.x in the body) -- grep confirms it. Per the batch reminder, an imported namespace never used as a term in the extracted lines stays an ordinary import, uncredited: reverted, RDF/DCTERMS/MD/Node/BNode/Literal are all left as plain rdflib imports (matching the source, which does not use them here either -- the sampled lines just happen to sit in a file that imports more than they need).

kgraphpy.namespaces.MD is genuinely project-owned but, for the same reason, gives this region nothing to credit for `from ... import p:` -- the construction the stratum is sampling for. The one thing the region DOES exercise from that import is collect_specific_namespaces, a function, not a namespace.

the copy loop `for triple in manifest_graph.triples((graph_uri, None, None)): header_graph.add(triple)` is the region's only real RDF operation: translated as `for @bindings in m{ {graph_uri} ?p ?o }(manifest_graph): +{ {graph_uri} ?p ?o }(header_graph)` -- a CONSTRUCT with no query engine, matching bindings.md's documented pattern exactly. Safe to fold into a join here because the original already iterates every match (not `.value`/`next`, so no cardinality change).

binding restoration: the extracted classmethod has no enclosing class (`cls` was free), so original.py/translated.ldpy both add a minimal CIMMetadataHeader (subject, graph only -- the other four __init__ parameters of the real class are never reached) plus `from_manifest = CIMMetadataHeader.from_manifest` at module level, identical on both sides. A duck-typed __eq__ (not isinstance-based: the two sides exec in separate namespaces, so "the same class" is two distinct objects) is scaffolding for comparability only, not business logic.

the zero-solution case (meta/oracle=values requires it) makes from_manifest RAISE ValueError, which the generic run_pair(entry=..., calls=[...]) cannot express -- any exception inside its call loop aborts the whole verdict as a driver error rather than a per-case outcome. driver.py is therefore custom (as edmondchuc__rdflib-orm's is, elsewhere in this same stratum): it calls from_manifest itself for a matching graph_uri and for a non-matching one, and compares outcome (returned vs raised, and the exception type) plus the returned object's subject/graph for the matching case.

context shim kgraphpy/ is a real two-level package (kgraphpy/namespaces.py) rather than a flat module, because the source does `from kgraphpy.namespaces import ...` -- a dotted import a flat shim module cannot satisfy. It works because rdfeval/check.py runs driver.py as a script with cwd=ex_dir, so Python puts ex_dir on sys.path[0] the way it does for any script's own directory.

optimization_notes: optimized.py: `Graph()` + `.parse(...)` chained (parse returns the graph); the add loop becomes `header_graph += manifest_graph.triples((graph_uri, None, None))` (Graph.__iadd__ is typed Iterable[triple] in rdflib 7.2.1); `len(header_graph) == 0` becomes `not header_graph`; the temporary NamespaceManager `nm` disappears: it is assigned to `header_graph.namespace_manager` first and the bindings go through `header_graph.bind(..., override=True)`, which delegates to that manager with the same arguments (driver: the header bindings compared on every case).

optimized.ldpy is identical to optimized.py: once the copy is a single `+=` over `graph.triples`, the translation's `for @bindings in m{ {graph_uri} ?p ?o }(manifest_graph): +{ {graph_uri} ?p ?o }(header_graph)` would be two lines and many more tokens, and no island yields whole triples to add in bulk. The rereading absorbs the region's only island; the notation brings nothing (ratio 1.0).
The CIMMetadataHeader scaffolding and the module-level alias are copied unchanged.
header_optimization_notes: Both header-variant files (identical): Node, RDF, BNode, Literal, DCTERMS and MD go; Path (annotation), Graph, URIRef, NamespaceManager and collect_specific_namespaces stay. NamespaceManager is not exported by the rdflib top-level package, so its import line cannot be merged.
